strings.title: The Thirteenth Floor
strings.hint: The hotel elevator has no thirteenth floor… but the stairs know the truth. And who holds the master maintenance card?
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: night hotel manager Bashir Helmi.

He ran a secret gambling room on the service floor between the twelfth and fourteenth floors, whose number "13" had been omitted. An accountant staying at the hotel discovered that the room numbers did not match the energy records and threatened to report it. Bashir lured him up the rear stairs with the promise of a "free room upgrade," strangled him on the service floor, then returned the body to his room and locked it with the master maintenance card to make it look as though he had died alone behind a locked door.

The maintenance card log showing his room opened at 03:12, the energy meter revealing a "nonexistent" floor, and a gambling chip in the victim's pocket bearing the secret room's emblem proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: In a luxury hotel whose elevator has no thirteenth-floor button out of superstition, a guest was found dead in his locked room on the fourteenth floor. The forensic examiner determined that he had been strangled, not died by suicide as it initially appeared. But the floor numbers do not lie: the energy meter records consumption in a space between floors that does not exist on the official plan.

strings.scene.address: Al-Nokhba Hotel — floor 14 and the omitted service floor
strings.scene.intro: A room apparently locked from the inside, but the master maintenance card can open any door without a trace. Between floors 12 and 14 is an unnumbered service space, its door disguised as a cupboard. Behind it are a gambling table and chairs for ten people.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The hidden service floor — as discovered
strings.scene.notes[1]: The energy meter records a floor absent from the plan
strings.scene.notes[2]: A master maintenance card opened the room at 03:12
strings.scene.notes[3]: An unusual gambling chip in the victim's pocket
strings.evidence[0].title: Master Maintenance Card
strings.evidence[0].desc: Opens every room; only the night manager carries it. It opened the victim's room at 03:12, after his death.
strings.evidence[1].title: Gambling Chip
strings.evidence[1].desc: Bears a unique emblem not found in any licensed casino: the "Floor 13 Club."
strings.evidence[2].title: Energy Meter Log
strings.evidence[2].desc: High nighttime consumption in a space between floors that does not appear on the hotel plan.
strings.evidence[3].title: The Victim's Notes
strings.evidence[3].desc: Room numbers and calculations that do not match the official hotel records. He had been quietly auditing them.
strings.evidence[4].title: The Disguised Cupboard Door
strings.evidence[4].found: End of the service floor corridor
strings.evidence[4].desc: A handle opens into the gambling room. It carries the manager's partial fingerprints.
strings.evidence[5].title: Emergency Stairwell Recording
strings.evidence[5].desc: At 02:40, the victim climbs toward the service floor with a man in a dark suit. The man's face is outside the frame.
strings.suspects[0].name: Fadi, the Neighboring Guest
strings.suspects[0].relation: His room is next to the victim's
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was asleep. My international calls prove I was in my room."
strings.suspects[0].statement: I heard a little commotion after midnight and assumed it was the air conditioning. I only knew the man well enough to greet him in the elevator. I'm here for a business deal and leave tomorrow. I have nothing to do with this hotel's mysteries.
strings.suspects[1].name: Bashir Helmi
strings.suspects[1].relation: Responsible for the floors at night
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I was at the reception desk all night. The camera can confirm it."
strings.suspects[1].statement: I've managed this hotel honorably for twelve years. The service floor is simply maintenance storage. Any talk of gambling is slander. My card is always with me. Perhaps I forgot to log a room visit for an air-conditioning complaint. Routine makes people forget.
strings.suspects[2].name: Samir, the Elevator Technician
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "My shift ended at ten in the evening and I left the building."
strings.suspects[2].statement: I know the elevator skips 13, and I know about the service floor. We all do. But I don't have its key. Only the manager does. I left early, and my exit card was logged at the gate.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Housekeeper
strings.witnesses[0].statement: The door appeared to be secured by the inside latch. But when I opened it with my card, I found the latch wasn't actually engaged, as if someone had used a trick to close it from outside.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Room Service Waiter
strings.witnesses[1].statement: Mr. Marwan ordered coffee at 23:30 and seemed anxious. He asked: "Is the floor above us haunted? Its number is strange." I laughed and told him there wasn't even a floor 13.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Parking Guard
strings.witnesses[2].statement: After three in the morning, I saw manager Bashir leave through the service door and return a quarter of an hour later, slightly out of breath. He said he had been chasing a cat that got into the storeroom.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Housekeeper's Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: A report of the death of the guest in room 1412. The door was locked and the scene initially suggested suicide.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Autopsy report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Manual strangulation from behind. The angle of the bruising completely rules out suicide. Death occurred between 02:30 and 03:00.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Body Movement Report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: Lividity analysis establishes that the body was moved from a different position after death. He did not die in his bed.
strings.folders[2].name: Records
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Door Access-Card Log
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: The master maintenance card opened room 1412 at 03:12, after the death. Its holder: the night manager.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Energy Meter Log
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: Regular nighttime consumption in an unnumbered space between 12 and 14, peaking after midnight.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Manager Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: His explanations for going out at night contradicted each other. No camera shows the "cat." He evaded questions about the service floor.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Neighboring Guest Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: His international calls place him in his room throughout the critical window.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Elevator Technician Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body: The staff gate confirms his departure at ten in the evening.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Raid on the Floor 13 Club
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: A gambling table, equipment, and a debt ledger were seized. The victim's name was listed as an "auditor who must be silenced."
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confession Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Confronted with the card log and the chip, the manager confessed: "He saw what he shouldn't have… I wanted to frighten him, not kill him."
strings.reports[0].title: Locked Room Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: The lock was a trick: a master card plus an unsecured latch. The murder happened on the service floor, then the body was returned.
strings.reports[1].title: Hidden Floor Report
strings.reports[1].author: Evidence department
strings.reports[1].body: The unnumbered space matches the gap in the energy records. Its only entrance requires the manager's card.
strings.notes[0].text: A nonexistent floor = a meter that does not lie
strings.notes[1].text: Who opened the dead man's room after his death?
